properties.name: MN-135 just south of Tower
properties.why: The last unfinished stretch of the Mesabi Trail — the trail still ends here; hikers walk MN-135.
properties.pano_note: Straight two-lane MN-135, narrow paved shoulder, dense pine forest both sides; no trail or sidewalk.

properties.name: MN-135, Wahlsten area
properties.why: The long, straight no-shoulder stretch hikers faced for ~15 mi before the trail was built — the "before" view.
properties.pano_note: Straight two-lane MN-135, narrow paved shoulder (thin asphalt strip beyond the white line, then grass/gravel), dense pine forest, cracked/repaired pavement; no trail.

properties.name: MN-135 at Embarrass
properties.why: South end of the old Embarrass–Tower gap, where the trail dead-ended ~6 mi short of Tower.
properties.pano_note: Winding two-lane MN-135, very narrow paved shoulder (white line at pavement edge, gravel/dirt beyond), dense forest; no trail on the road. Mesabi Trail crosses MN-135 here.

properties.name: MN-169, Eagles Nest area
properties.why: The contrast shot: rebuilt 2018 — what a rebuilt highway looks like. (Keypoints 2024 shows mostly 4-ft paved shoulders here, not a uniform 8 ft.)
properties.pano_note: Two-lane MN-169, wide paved (concrete) shoulder on both sides in the rotated view, pine forest, lake glimpsed through trees; no separate trail.

properties.name: MN-169 / E. Sheridan St, Ely
properties.why: East end of the Mesabi Trail, where the NCT continues east on Fernberg Rd toward Kawishiwi Falls.
properties.pano_note: Pano ~20 m south of the point, same street. Urban E Sheridan St / Voyageur Hwy: curbs and sidewalks, brick building, person on sidewalk; no highway shoulder (urban section).

properties.name: US-75 at Kent
properties.why: Two-lane US highway, narrow-to-no shoulder — the most exposed highway stretch on the western route.
properties.pano_note: Straight two-lane US-75, narrow gravel shoulders beyond the white edge lines, flat farmland both sides; no trail, no sidewalk — the most exposed spot in the check.

properties.name: CR-88 southeast of Rothsay
properties.why: Northwest end of the 15.8-mi CR-88 stretch; paved county road, farm traffic.
properties.pano_note: Nearest pano ~238 m north-west of the point, same road. Two-lane Co Rd 88, very narrow paved shoulder, flat soybean fields, Rothsay grain silos and water tower ahead; no trail.

properties.name: CR-88 at Fergus Falls
properties.why: Where the CR-88 road walk reaches town.
properties.pano_note: Junction of CR-88 and Maryland Ln: wide paved residential road with curb/gutter and grass verges; no trail on the county road in view.

properties.name: US-59, Fergus Falls
properties.why: The route crosses I-94, US-59 and the Pelican River in close succession — the highest-traffic crossing on the corridor.
properties.pano_note: US-59 southbound (signed Purple Heart Trail), wide paved shoulder on the right, semi-truck ahead, I-94 signs in the distance; no trail.

properties.name: MN-210 E, Fergus Falls
properties.why: Trunk highway through east Fergus Falls; the Central Lakes Trail trailhead sits on Hwy 210.
properties.pano_note: MN-210 East (Otter Trail Scenic Byway), two-lane with a wide paved shoulder, plant nursery / storage buildings across the road; no trail.

properties.name: ND-4 / Fort Abercrombie
properties.why: The Red River crossing: road-walk Minnesota meets off-road trail in North Dakota.
properties.pano_note: NO panorama on ND-4 at the point. Nearest pano ~180 m west is INSIDE Fort Abercrombie State Historic Site grounds (log cabin, split-rail fence, gravel path); no highway shown. Do not present as a road view.
